subject: Urgent: Traffic reshuffle and temporary region reroute (US / EU / APAC)
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme-ml.com>, Elena Petrov <elena@bankingcorp.com>
Cc: Platform Ops <platform-ops@acme-ml.com>
Date: 2028-02-13T08:15:00Z
Subject: Urgent: Traffic reshuffle and temporary region reroute (US / EU / APAC)

Hi Sanjay, Elena —

Quick note: we detected a partial degradation affecting a subset of edge clusters in three cloud regions (US East, Frankfurt, and APAC-SIN). Starting now we are shifting customer traffic away from the impacted cells to healthy cells in the same region where possible; for BankingCorp we are also enabling cross-region fallback to avoid request failures.

What this means for you:
- Short window (expected 15–45m) of increased latency for in-flight requests while connections re-establish.
- No data loss; all requests are being proxied and retried.
- For some customers with very strict affinity, we will route to Dedicated capacity in a different region as a temporary safety valve (we'll notify if we flip your routing).

Immediate asks:
1) Please confirm if you have any strict IP allowlists or private network constraints that would block cross-region routing.
2) If you see an error 503 or persistent latency > 3s for more than 20 minutes, reply and we'll escalate to a live bridge.

We're publishing live updates here: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2028-0213

Attachments: small reroute map and the playbook we used for the diversion.

I'll follow up with a post-incident note once we have a root cause and timeline.

—Avery

Subject: Internal: BankingCorp — allowlist / temporary routing plan (INC-2028-0213)

Team —

BankingCorp has allowlists for FR and US-EAST only. Sanjay flagged that APAC routing would fail their firewall. Options:
1) Keep routing within region where possible (we already moved traffic to healthy cells in FR and US-EAST).
2) If capacity in-region degrades further, escalate to Dedicated cross-region failover; this will present different IPs (we must notify customer and coordinate allowlist updates).

Action items:
- Marissa: prepare a short customer note with the two IP ranges we would use for a Dedicated fallback and an opt-in toggle. Sanjay needs this within 30m.
- Dylan: measure prefix-level latency for BankingCorp flows and confirm whether KV cache warmup time will risk higher 503s during the reroute. If yes, provide mitigation (prefetch, sticky-sidecar).
- Sean: update the public incident page and mark the regions impacted. Add the reroute map from the attachments.

I'm starting a bridged Slack huddle; if we decide to flip to Dedicated, I'll call the customer.

—Avery

From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-02-13T08:38:00Z
Subject: Re: Internal: BankingCorp — allowlist / temporary routing plan (INC-2028-0213)

Quick tech note — observed behavior and recommendation:
- KV cache drop observed when we move traffic off an edge cell; cold-start penalty ~120–300ms per session for their typical token lengths.
- For BankingCorp use-case (short prompt, latency-sensitive), I recommend:
  * Enable sticky-sidecar for 30m after cutover to preserve warmed caches where possible.
  * Increase short-tail batch timeout from 8ms to 12ms to keep latency variance bounded during the shift.
  * If we flip to Dedicated, pre-warm model KV cache by replaying last 1k unique user prefixes (we have their consent logs).

I'll post the latency scrape in Slack and attach the micro-timeline.

—Dylan
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-02-16T17:50:00Z
Subject: Post-incident summary: Partial edge disruption and traffic reshuffle (INC-2028-0213)

Team / Sanjay / Elena —

Post-incident summary (concise):
- Incident window: 2028-02-13T07:58Z — 2028-02-13T12:30Z (initial detection at ~07:58Z).
- Impact: transient increased latency and intermittent 503s for a subset of customers pinned to three edge clusters (US-EAST, eu-central, apac-sin). BankingCorp saw a median latency bump of +180ms and 0.4% transient error rate during the peak.
- Root cause (interim): a mis-propagated kernel upgrade at our cloud provider caused degraded packet processing on a small subset of NICs tied to specific edge cells. Provider confirmed a roll-forward rollback fixed the NIC flaps. We are awaiting their final RCA.
- Mitigation steps we executed:
  1) Automated traffic diversion to healthy cells in-region (immediate).
  2) Applied sticky-sidecar and adjusted batching windows for latency-sensitive flows (Dylan).
  3) Offered Dedicated fallback to customers with strict affinity; BankingCorp declined after we provided IP ranges.
  4) Continuous monitoring and 30m cadence customer updates.

Follow-ups / action items (owner + ETA):
- Provider RCA capture and distribution (Avery, 2028-02-20).
- Add a safety gate to our kernel rollout checks to detect NIC metrics anomalies pre-deploy (Dylan, 2028-03-02).
- Improve customer-facing allowlist docs with a one-click policy flow (Marissa, 2028-02-23).
- Add a runbook entry that prescribes sticky-sidecar + pre-warm prefixes for latency-critical customers during region reroutes (Sean, 2028-02-24).

Attachments: incident_timeline.csv (detailed request-level traces), reroute_playbook_v1.pdf (what we executed), reroute map.

If you want a full postmortem write-up for BankingCorp (formatted for legal/compliance), say the word and we'll prepare it.

Thanks all for the fast coordination.

—Avery

Redwood Inference
